page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY processor cores running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports several advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI) and cryptography acceleration via AES. These hardware flags assist with vector calculations and encryption tasks. The processor features a 35 MB L3 cache, alongside 1.0 MB L2 and 32 KB L1d caches per core, supporting hyper-threading topology.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6986.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 8224.85. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1140.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1312.09. Memory bandwidth remains average, reaching 49.44 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 36.78 GB/sec for large block write operations. Conversely, static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations fall into the lower performance tier.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers a structured compute-to-memory profile suitable for workloads that require consistent CPU access without massive memory footprints. It is appropriate for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, and moderate database operations. However, the lack of local storage and lower single-threaded performance suggest it is less suited for high-throughput web serving or memory-intensive caching layers.
